title: Carriers and insurtechs move onto our turf

tldr.text: Cobaltrock Mutual launched SafeSight, a free camera pilot for its larger policyholders. Lead with data ownership: SafeSight's findings stay with the carrier.
Watchpost AI now sells lift and posture scoring (Ergo), so ergonomics is no longer a clean win. Shift to OSHA, broker reporting and edge blurring.
Pennant Comp has new CFO and CRO hires and a sales reorg. Its customers are asking about leaving at renewal; ask your broker contacts who's up next.

trends.summary: Camera-based safety is going mainstream, and the companies selling it are spreading from safety teams to insurers.

items.text: Two carriers in our fictional market launched or piloted computer-vision programs for policyholders this month. Expect buyers to ask whether their carrier's free option is good enough.
Ergonomics add-ons are now table stakes for AI safety vendors. Differentiation is shifting to what happens after the alert: coaching, OSHA paperwork and renewal reporting.

regulatory.summary: No new federal rules, but state privacy rules on workplace video keep tightening.

items.text: A state workplace-surveillance bill advanced that would require notice before employers analyze video of workers. Our edge blurring and worker notice already meet the draft language.

mna.summary: One carrier merger and one insurtech acquisition.

items.text: Ferncliff Insurance Group agreed to merge with Ardent Re, closing Q2 2027. Ferncliff policyholders face a year of service changes.
Riskloom bought claims-analytics startup Fennel, deepening its carrier-side claims product. It still doesn't sell to employers.

health.summary: Workers' comp remains profitable for carriers, which keeps rates soft and makes price-only pitches easy to make.

items.text: Soft rates mean prospects feel less premium pain. Lead with claim frequency and lost workdays, not only premium.

movers.name: Watchpost AI
movers.whatChanged: Launched Watchpost Ergo for lift and posture scoring and rewrote the homepage around deployment speed.
movers.soWhat: Don't lead with ergonomics against Watchpost anymore. Lead with OSHA recordkeeping, the broker report and edge blurring, none of which Ergo touches.

movers.name: Liftwise Labs
movers.whatChanged: Published per-worker pricing for the first time.
movers.soWhat: A visible per-worker price makes the total easy to compare. Do the math for the prospect's headcount, including temps who also need devices.

movers.name: Pennant Comp
movers.whatChanged: Replaced its CFO and CRO, reorganized sales, and its employee rating dropped.
movers.soWhat: Pennant customers are open to a conversation. Pitch Keelstone as the way to keep the safety results while going back to the carrier they had before.

movers.name: Riskloom
movers.soWhat: No change to how we sell. Riskloom is carrier-side; if a prospect mentions it, the point is that our broker report gives their underwriter newer evidence.

movers.name: Tally Comp
movers.whatChanged: Opened eligibility to employers with up to 250 employees in 12 states.
movers.soWhat: Tally will start showing up in mid-market deals. Ask whether the prospect wants to keep its broker and carrier; Tally requires leaving both.

movers.name: Cobaltrock Mutual
movers.whatChanged: Announced SafeSight, a camera-based safety pilot for selected policyholders, and is promoting AI safety on its homepage.
movers.soWhat: Ask who owns SafeSight's findings if the customer changes carriers. Keelstone data belongs to the employer and goes with them to renewal.

movers.name: Ferncliff Insurance Group
movers.whatChanged: Announced a merger with Ardent Re, closing Q2 2027.
movers.soWhat: Ferncliff policyholders will see service and contact changes. Lead with continuity: our coverage doesn't change when their loss-control team does.

movers.name: Tidewater State Fund
movers.whatChanged: Safety grants will cover AI safety technology starting in 2027.
movers.soWhat: Good news for us: Tidewater policyholders can put grant money toward Keelstone. Mention it in every Tidewater deal.
